_readme: Single source of truth for the SEO loop's caps, thresholds and fences. Read by seo/scripts/*. Changing this file is an owner-only act: seo/ is GUARDED in ci.yml, so an agent PR that touches it fails build-chain-guard. Brief values are kept verbatim; every deviation carries a `_why` that points at the measured reason (see seo/ARCHITECTURE.md §Deviations).

caps._why_files_lines: Blast-radius backstop on top of the brief's page cap: one dataset edit can re-render many URLs, so verify-build also counts rendered URLs that changed.

gates._why_crawlStall: No newly listed URL was crawled between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-27 and 20 sitemap URLs are 'URL is unknown to Google'. New URLs join a queue Google is not draining, so gap articles wait until it moves.

thresholds._why_persistence: Week-to-week overlap of the striking-distance set was 0.56-0.67 (Jaccard) across six snapshots; persistence keeps the loop from editing pages that only qualified by noise.

brakes._why_siteWide_floor: Site-wide clicks were 13-29 per 28 days (3-7 a week). A 20% drop is one click; without a floor the brake would halt the loop in roughly 40% of weeks on noise.

outcomes._why_neutralBand: A placebo split of the striking-distance pages (20,000 random splits, no treatment) showed a 95th-percentile gap of x3.83-3.93 between halves over 56 days. Anything inside that band is labelled neutral, not win or loss.

_why_excluded: Legal, billing, analyzer and hub pages are off-limits to scheduled runs (brief), and the hubs plus /about, /why-truecap, /sample-decision-memo and the spreadsheet have exact titles pinned by lib/__tests__/public-metadata-contract.test.ts.
_why_domains: Outbound links an agent adds must land on a primary source. State statute, county assessor and city licensing domains are added here by the owner as markets are enriched (never by the model).
_why_vendorDomains: A competitor claim on a /vs page must link the vendor's own dated page (its pricing or feature page). These hosts are allowed ONLY in app/vs/*/page.tsx files, only at tier 1, and only for competitor claims; they are never a source for a tax, legal or market fact.

sweepCommits._readme: Commits that touched (nearly) every page for presentation-only reasons (vocabulary, identity, header, lint/format, runtime). lastmod seeding skips them; a URL's date is the newest non-sweep commit that changed its own content or data. These SHAs are sweeps that were already on main; a SHA must be in the seeded history (`lastmod.ts seed` refuses to run when one is not, and names the landed copy of a rebased commit). A NEW sweep marks itself instead with a `Lastmod-Sweep: true` trailer in its commit message, which survives rebases, cherry-picks and GitHub's rebase-merge (F1, the unnamed author, and F4's structured-data commits and their review fixes carry it).

ctrCurve._readme: Approximate organic CTR by average position, used ONLY to rank opportunities relative to each other. Never published as a fact.

_primarySourceDomainsWhy: Federal domains are listed for clarity; "gov" admits every .gov host (subdomains of gov), because only US federal, state, local and tribal governments can register a .gov name, so a county assessor or a city's rental-licensing page is a primary source. Added 2026-09-28 after the fifth live run skipped every market-enrich candidate for lack of county/city domains (#136). Non-.gov government sites (e.g. a county appraisal district on .org) are still added one by one, by the owner.
